title.zh: 卷二百二十五 列傳第一百十三 張瀚 王國光 梁夢龍 楊巍 李戴 趙煥 鄭繼之
title.en: Volume 225 Biographies 113: Zhang Han, Wang Guoguang, Liang Menglong, Yang Wei, Li Dai, Zhao Huan, Zheng Jizhi
title.raw: 卷二百二十五 列傳第一百十三 張瀚 王國光 梁夢龍 楊巍 李戴 趙煥 鄭繼之 Volume 225 Biographies 113: Zhang Han, Wang Guoguang, Liang Menglong, Yang Wei, Li Dai, Zhao Huan, Zheng Jizhi

sentences.zh: 張瀚王國光梁夢龍楊巍李戴趙煥鄭繼之

translations.literal: Zhang Han, Wang Guoguang, Liang Menglong, Yang Wei, Li Dai, Zhao Huan, Zheng Jizhi
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han, Wang Guoguang, Liang Menglong, Yang Wei, Li Dai, Zhao Huan, and Zheng Jizhi

sentences.zh: 張瀚，字子文，仁和人。

translations.literal: Zhang Han, style Ziwen, was a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han, courtesy name Ziwen, came from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fourteenth year of the Jiajing reign (1535).

sentences.zh: 授南京工部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 歷廬州知府，改大名。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Luzhou, then was transferred to Daming.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as prefect of Luzhou, he was transferred to Daming.

sentences.zh: 俺答圍京師，詔遣兵部郎中征畿輔民兵入衛。

translations.literal: When Altan besieged the capital, an edict sent a bureau director from the Ministry of War to levy militia from the capital region for defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan Khan besieged the capital, an imperial edict dispatched a bureau director from the Ministry of War to raise militia from the capital region for its defense.

sentences.zh: 瀚立閱戶籍，三十丁簡一人，而以二十九人供其餉，得八百人。

translations.literal: Han immediately reviewed household registers, selecting one man from every thirty households and having the other twenty-nine supply his provisions, thus obtaining eight hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Han at once examined household registers, drafting one man from every thirty households while having the remaining twenty-nine households supply his rations, and in this way raised eight hundred troops.

sentences.zh: 馳至真定，請使者閱兵，使者稱其才。

translations.literal: He hastened to Zhending and asked the envoy to review the troops; the envoy praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried to Zhending and invited the envoy to inspect the troops, and the envoy commended his capability.

sentences.zh: 累遷陜西左布政使，擢右副都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to left provincial administration commissioner of Shaanxi and then elevated to right vice censor-in-chief, administering that region as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to become left provincial administration commissioner of Shaanxi, then was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief with authority to administer the province.

sentences.zh: 甫半歲，入為大理卿。

translations.literal: After only half a year he entered the capital as president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Barely half a year later he was summoned to the capital as president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 進刑部右侍郎，俄改兵部，總督漕運。

translations.literal: He advanced to right vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments, then soon was transferred to the Ministry of War and appointed grand coordinator of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments, then shortly afterward transferred to the Ministry of War and placed in charge of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 萬歷元年，吏部尚書楊博罷，召瀚代之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli, Minister of Personnel Yang Bo was dismissed and Han was summoned to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wanli reign (1573), Minister of Personnel Yang Bo was removed, and Han was called to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When his term was completed, he was given the additional title of junior guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, he was granted the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時廷推吏部尚書，首左都御史葛守禮，次工部尚書朱衡，次瀚。

translations.literal: At that time in court recommendation for Minister of Personnel, the Left Censor-in-Chief Ge Shouli was first, Minister of Works Zhu Heng second, and Han third.
translations.idiomatic: When the court recommended candidates for Minister of Personnel, Ge Shouli, the Left Censor-in-Chief, ranked first, Zhu Heng, Minister of Works, second, and Han third.

sentences.zh: 居正惡守禮戇，厭衡驕，故特拔瀚。

translations.literal: Juzheng detested Shouli's bluntness and was weary of Heng's arrogance, so he specially elevated Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng disliked Ge Shouli's obstinacy and was tired of Zhu Heng's arrogance, and therefore singled out Han for promotion.

sentences.zh: 瀚資望淺，忽見擢，舉朝益趨事居正，而瀚進退大臣率奉居正指。

translations.literal: Han's qualifications and standing were shallow; upon this sudden promotion the whole court increasingly rushed to serve Juzheng, while Han in promoting and demoting great ministers generally followed Juzheng's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Han's seniority and reputation were slight, and after this abrupt elevation the entire court leaned ever more toward Zhang Juzheng; in advancing and retiring high ministers, Han generally followed Juzheng's wishes.

sentences.zh: 即出己意，輿論多不協。

translations.literal: Even when he expressed his own views, public opinion mostly did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Even when he ventured his own opinion, public sentiment usually did not align with it.

sentences.zh: 以是為御史鄭準、王希元所劾。

translations.literal: For this he was impeached by censors Zheng Zhun and Wang Xiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On this account he was impeached by the investigating censors Zheng Zhun and Wang Xiyuan.

sentences.zh: 居正顧之厚，不納也。

translations.literal: Juzheng looked upon him with great favor and did not accept the charges.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng regarded him favorably and would not allow the impeachments to stand.

sentences.zh: 御史劉臺劾居正，因論瀚撫陜狼籍，又唯諾居正狀。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Tai impeached Juzheng and in the same memorial discussed Han's chaotic administration in Shaanxi and his manner of simply agreeing with Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Liu Tai impeached Zhang Juzheng, he also criticized Han's disorderly rule in Shaanxi and his habit of assenting to whatever Juzheng wanted.

sentences.zh: 比居正遭喪，謀奪情，瀚心非之。

translations.literal: When Juzheng encountered a bereavement, they schemed to have him retain office during mourning; Han inwardly disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng's father died and a plan was made for him to remain in office instead of observing mourning, Han opposed it in his heart.

sentences.zh: 中旨令瀚諭留居正，居正又自為牘，風瀚屬吏，以覆旨請。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript ordered Han to instruct that Juzheng be retained; Juzheng also wrote a memorial himself and hinted to Han's subordinates that they should request a reply to the rescript.
translations.idiomatic: A rescript from the throne directed Han to urge that Juzheng be kept in post; Juzheng also drafted his own memorial and signaled to Han's staff that they should seek an imperial response.

sentences.zh: 瀚佯不喻，謂「政府奔喪，宜予殊典，禮部事也，何關吏部。

translations.literal: Han pretended not to understand and said, "When the chief minister hurries home for mourning, an extraordinary favor should be granted—that is a matter for the Ministry of Rites; what has it to do with the Ministry of Personnel?"
translations.idiomatic: Han feigned incomprehension, saying, "When the chief minister rushes home for a parent's funeral, an exceptional dispensation should be granted—that concerns the Ministry of Rites. What business is it of the Ministry of Personnel?"

sentences.zh: 」居正復令客說之，不為動，乃傳旨責瀚久不奉詔，無人臣禮。

translations.literal: Juzheng again had a guest persuade him, but Han was unmoved; then a rescript was transmitted rebuking Han for long failing to obey the edict and lacking the decorum of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng sent another intermediary to persuade him, but Han would not budge; finally a rescript censured him for having long defied the imperial order and lacking the deportment owed a minister.

sentences.zh: 廷臣惴恐，交章留居正，瀚獨不與，撫膺太息曰：「三綱淪矣！

translations.literal: Court officials were fearful; they submitted memorial after memorial to retain Juzheng; Han alone did not join them and, striking his breast, sighed deeply: "The three cardinal bonds are ruined!"
translations.idiomatic: The officials at court were terrified and memorialized one after another to keep Zhang Juzheng in office; Han alone would not add his name. Clasping his chest, he sighed: "The three bonds of society are undone!"

sentences.zh: 」居正怒，嗾給事中王道成、御史謝思啟摭他事劾之，勒致仕歸。

translations.literal: Juzheng was angry and instigated supervising secretaries Wang Daocheng and censor Xie Siqi to gather other matters to impeach him, forcing him to retire and return home.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Zhang Juzheng prompted the supervising secretaries Wang Daocheng and the censor Xie Siqi to dredge up other charges against him and compelled him to resign and retire.

sentences.zh: 居正歿，帝頗念瀚。

translations.literal: After Juzheng's death the emperor came to think rather often of Han.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Juzheng died, the emperor came to miss Han.

sentences.zh: 詔有司給月廩，年及八十，特賜存問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to grant him a monthly stipend; when he reached eighty he was specially favored with an imperial inquiry after his health.
translations.idiomatic: An edict instructed the appropriate agencies to supply him a monthly allowance, and when he turned eighty the throne sent a special message asking after his welfare.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保，謚恭懿。

translations.literal: Upon his death he was posthumously given the title of junior guardian of the heir apparent and the posthumous name Gongyi.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Gongyi ("Respectful and Benevolent").

sentences.zh: 王國光，字汝觀，陽城人。

translations.literal: Wang Guoguang, style Ruguan, was a native of Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guoguang, courtesy name Ruguan, came from Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jiajing he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-third year of the Jiajing reign (1544).

sentences.zh: 授吳江知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 鄰邑有疑獄來質，訊輒得情。

translations.literal: When a neighboring county had a doubtful case and came to consult him, upon interrogation he always got at the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring counties brought doubtful cases to him for judgment, and his interrogations invariably uncovered the facts.

sentences.zh: 調儀封，擢兵部主事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yifeng, then promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After transfer to Yifeng he was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 改吏部，歷文選郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and served through the post of bureau director of civil appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Ministry of Personnel and rose to bureau director of civil appointments.

sentences.zh: 屢遷戶部右侍郎，總督倉場。

translations.literal: After repeated promotions he became right vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue and was appointed grand coordinator of the granary depots.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he became right vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue and was placed in charge of the granary depots.

sentences.zh: 謝病去。

translations.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年，起刑部左侍郎，拜南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing he was recalled as left vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments and appointed Minister of Punishments at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Longqing reign (1570) he was recalled as left vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments and appointed Minister of Punishments at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 未上，改戶部，再督倉場。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and again put in charge of the granary depots.
translations.idiomatic: Before he assumed that office he was shifted to the Ministry of Revenue and again placed over the granary depots.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，還理部事。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, he returned to manage the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shenzong Emperor came to the throne, he resumed direct management of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 時簿牒繁冗，自州縣達部，有繕書、輸解、交納諸費，公私苦之。

translations.literal: At that time documents were numerous and cumbersome; from prefectures and counties up to the ministry there were fees for copying, transport, delivery, and payment, to the distress of public and private alike.
translations.idiomatic: Records had become voluminous and burdensome: from the counties and prefectures up to the ministry, charges for copying, transport, delivery, and payment afflicted both government and populace.

sentences.zh: 國光疏請裁並，去繁文十三四，時稱簡便。

translations.literal: Guoguang memorialized requesting consolidation and elimination, removing three or four tenths of the redundant paperwork, and at the time it was praised as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguang submitted a memorial asking that procedures be consolidated, cutting redundant paperwork by roughly a third to a half, and contemporaries hailed the reform as a welcome simplification.

sentences.zh: 戶部十三司，自弘治來，以公署隘，惟郎中一人治事，員外郎、主事止除官日一赴而已。

translations.literal: The thirteen bureaus of the Ministry of Revenue, since the Hongzhi reign because the public offices were cramped, had only the bureau director handling affairs; vice directors and principal clerks came only once on the day of their appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Hongzhi reign the thirteen bureaus of the Ministry of Revenue, cramped for space, had been run by the bureau director alone; vice directors and principal clerks appeared only once, on the day they received appointment.

sentences.zh: 郎中力不給，則委之吏胥，弊益滋。

translations.literal: When the director's strength was insufficient, matters were delegated to clerks and runners, and abuses increased all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When the director could not cope, work was handed to clerks and runners, and malfeasance only grew worse.

sentences.zh: 國光盡令入署，職務得修舉。

translations.literal: Guoguang ordered them all into the offices, and duties were properly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguang required them all to work in the offices, and official business was once again properly conducted.

sentences.zh: 邊餉告匱，而諸邊歲出及屯田、鹽課無可稽。

translations.literal: Frontier provisions reported shortage, yet annual expenditures of the various frontiers together with garrison farms and salt levies had nothing by which they could be checked.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier supplies were said to be exhausted, yet there was no reliable accounting of yearly outlays on the borders, garrison farming, or salt revenues.

sentences.zh: 國光請敕邊臣核實，且畫經久策以聞。

translations.literal: Guoguang requested an edict ordering frontier officials to verify accounts and also to draft a long-term plan to report.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguang asked that frontier officials be ordered to verify the figures and submit a durable long-term plan.

sentences.zh: 甘肅巡撫廖逢節等各條上其數，耗蠹為損。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator of Gansu Liao Fengjie and others each itemized and reported their figures, and waste and corruption were thereby reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coordinator of Gansu, Liao Fengjie, and others each submitted detailed accounts, and waste and corruption were curbed as a result.

sentences.zh: 萬歷元年，奏言：「國初，天下州縣存留夏稅秋糧可一千二百萬石。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli he memorialized, saying: "At the beginning of the dynasty, the grain retained in prefectures and counties from summer tax and autumn grain could amount to about twelve million piculs."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wanli he memorialized: "At the founding of the dynasty, the grain retained locally by prefectures and counties from summer tax and autumn grain payments came to roughly twelve million piculs."

sentences.zh: 其時議主寬大，歲用外，計贏銀百萬有余。

translations.literal: At that time policy favored leniency; apart from annual expenditure, surplus silver was calculated at more than a million taels.
translations.idiomatic: Policy then favored leniency; beyond yearly expenditures, the surplus in silver was reckoned at more than a million taels.

sentences.zh: 使有司歲征無缺，則州縣積貯自豐，水旱盜賊不能為災患。

translations.literal: If the local offices collected each year without shortfall, then prefectures and counties would naturally have abundant stores, and flood, drought, or bandits could not become calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Had local officials collected the full levy every year, county and prefectural granaries would have stayed full, and flood, drought, or banditry could not have brought disaster.

sentences.zh: 今一遘兵荒，輒留京儲，發內帑。

translations.literal: Now at the first encounter of war or famine, capital reserves are immediately retained and the inner treasury is opened.
translations.idiomatic: Today, at the first sign of war or famine, capital reserves are seized and the imperial privy purse is tapped.

sentences.zh: 由有司視存留甚緩，茍事催科，則謂擾民，弊遂至此。

translations.literal: Because local offices regarded retained grain as very lax—if they pressed collection they were said to harass the people—abuses reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Because local officials treated retained grain as a low priority and called vigorous collection harassment of the people, the system has decayed to its present state.

sentences.zh: 請行天下撫按官，督所司具報出入、存留、逋負之數，臣部得通融會計，以其余濟邊。

translations.literal: He requested that grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners throughout the empire supervise their subordinates in reporting figures for receipts, disbursements, retained grain, and arrears, so that his ministry could make flexible calculations and use the surplus to aid the frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners nationwide require full reports of receipts, disbursements, retained grain, and arrears, so his ministry could balance accounts flexibly and apply the surplus to frontier needs.

sentences.zh: 有司催征不力者，悉以新令從事。

translations.literal: Local offices that were lax in pressing collection should all be dealt with under the new regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who failed to press collection vigorously should all be held to the new rules.

sentences.zh: 」制可。

translations.literal: " The imperial decision approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 京軍支糧通州者，候伺甚艱。

translations.literal: Capital troops drawing grain rations at Tongzhou waited in great hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Capital garrison troops who drew rations at Tongzhou endured long, painful waits.

sentences.zh: 國光請遣部郎一人司之，名坐糧廳，投牒驗發，無過三日，諸軍便之。

translations.literal: Guoguang requested that one bureau director from the ministry be sent to manage it, called the Ration-Issuing Office; upon presenting a slip and verification, issuance took no more than three days, to the convenience of all troops.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguang proposed dispatching a bureau director to oversee the office, named the Ration Desk; troops presented their vouchers, received verification, and were issued grain within three days—a great relief to the garrison.

sentences.zh: 天下錢谷散隸諸司，國光請歸並責成：畿輔府州縣歸福建司，南畿歸四川司，鹽課歸山東司，關稅歸貴州司，淮、徐、臨、德諸倉歸雲南司，禦馬、象房及二十四馬房芻料歸廣西司。

translations.literal: Revenue and grain throughout the empire were scattered under various bureaus; Guoguang requested consolidation with clear responsibility: capital-region prefectures and counties to the Fujian Bureau, the southern capital region to the Sichuan Bureau, salt levies to the Shandong Bureau, customs duties to the Guizhou Bureau, granaries at Huai, Xu, Lin, and De to the Yunnan Bureau, and fodder for the imperial stables, elephant quarters, and twenty-four horse quarters to the Guangxi Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue and grain accounts were scattered across many bureaus; Guoguang asked that they be consolidated with clear lines of responsibility: the capital region under the Fujian Bureau, the southern metropolitan area under Sichuan, salt under Shandong, customs under Guizhou, the Huai, Xu, Lin, and De granaries under Yunnan, and fodder for the imperial horse stables, elephant quarters, and twenty-four remount depots under Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 遂為定制。

translations.literal: This then became a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: These arrangements became permanent regulations.

sentences.zh: 三年，京察拾遺。

translations.literal: In the third year, in the capital evaluation he was picked out for censure.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was singled out for censure in the capital officials' evaluation.

sentences.zh: 國光為南京給事、御史所劾。

translations.literal: Guoguang was impeached by Nanjing supervising secretaries and censors.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguang was impeached by supervising secretaries and censors at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 再疏乞罷，帝特留之。

translations.literal: He memorialized again asking to resign; the emperor specially retained him.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again asking to be dismissed, but the emperor expressly kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 明年復固以請，乃詔乘傳歸。

translations.literal: The next year he again firmly requested; then an edict ordered him to return home by imperial post.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he pressed the request again, and an edict allowed him to return home with post-horses provided.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，以所輯條例名《萬歷會計錄》上之。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he presented the regulations he had compiled, entitled Records of Wanli Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving office he submitted the regulations he had compiled under the title Records of Wanli Accounts.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其留心國計，令戶部訂正。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his attention to national finance and ordered the Ministry of Revenue to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his care for state finances and ordered the Ministry of Revenue to revise the work.

sentences.zh: 及書成，詔褒諭焉。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, an edict praised and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was finished, an edict commended him with imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，吏部尚書張瀚罷，起國光代。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year, Minister of Personnel Zhang Han was dismissed and Guoguang was recalled to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter in the fifth year, Minister of Personnel Zhang Han was removed and Guoguang was recalled to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 陳采實政、別繁簡、責守令、恤卑官、罷加納數事，皆允行。

translations.literal: He presented matters of assessing substantive policy, distinguishing the cumbersome from the simple, holding prefects and magistrates accountable, showing compassion to low officials, and abolishing supplemental payments—all were approved and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed reforms on evaluating substantive governance, separating essential from redundant procedures, holding prefects and magistrates accountable, easing burdens on junior officials, and ending supplemental surcharges—all of which were approved.

sentences.zh: 尋以考績，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon, on the basis of performance evaluation, he was given the additional title of grand guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, on the strength of his performance review, he was granted the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 八年，當考察外吏，請毋限日期。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when it was time to evaluate outer officials, he requested that no date limit be imposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when outer officials were due for evaluation, he asked that no fixed deadline be imposed.

sentences.zh: 詔許之，且命詿誤者聽從公辯雪。

translations.literal: An edict approved this and also ordered that those who had erred through misunderstanding be allowed to clear themselves by public debate.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed and also allowed officials who had erred through misunderstanding to defend themselves openly and clear their names.

sentences.zh: 明年大計京朝官，徇張居正意，置吳中行等五人於察籍。

translations.literal: The next year in the great evaluation of capital officials, following Zhang Juzheng's wishes, he placed Wu Zhonghang and four others on the censure register.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the major evaluation of capital officials, he followed Zhang Juzheng's wishes and placed Wu Zhonghang and four others on the censure list.

sentences.zh: 國光有才智。

translations.literal: Guoguang had talent and intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguang was talented and capable.

sentences.zh: 初掌邦計，多所建白。

translations.literal: When he first managed national accounts he made many proposals.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took charge of national finances he offered many constructive proposals.

sentences.zh: 及是受制執政，聲名損於初。

translations.literal: By this time, constrained by the chief minister, his reputation suffered compared with the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: By then, hemmed in by the chief minister, his reputation fell short of what it had been at first.

sentences.zh: 給事中商尚忠論國光銓選私所親，而給事中張世則出為河南僉事，憾國光，劾其鬻官黷貨。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Shang Shangzhong criticized Guoguang for favoring his private associates in appointments; supervising secretary Zhang Shize, having gone out as Henan vice commissioner and bearing a grudge against Guoguang, impeached him for selling offices and corrupt gain.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Shang Shangzhong accused Guoguang of staffing appointments with his own favorites; Zhang Shize, a supervising secretary who had been sent out as vice commissioner of Henan and resented Guoguang, impeached him for selling offices and taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 國光再奏辯，帝再慰留，責世則挾私，貶儀真丞。

translations.literal: Guoguang memorialized again in defense; the emperor again comforted and retained him, rebuked Shize for private motives, and demoted him to assistant magistrate of Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguang memorialized again in his own defense; the emperor again urged him to stay, blamed Shize for acting from private spite, and demoted him to assistant magistrate of Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 及居正卒，御史楊寅秋劾國光六罪。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, censor Yang Yinqiu impeached Guoguang on six charges.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Juzheng died, Censor Yang Yinqiu impeached Guoguang on six counts.

sentences.zh: 帝遂怒，落職閑住。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon grew angry and stripped him of office to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered and removed him from office to live in idleness.

sentences.zh: 已，念其勞，命復官致仕。

translations.literal: Later, remembering his labors, the emperor ordered his rank restored and permitted him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Later, mindful of his service, the emperor restored his rank and allowed him to retire with honors.

sentences.zh: 梁夢龍，字乾吉，真定人。

translations.literal: Liang Menglong, style Qianji, was a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Menglong, courtesy name Qianji, came from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十二年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Jiajing he became a jinshi and was made a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the thirty-second year of the Jiajing reign (1553) and was appointed a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 授兵科給事中，首劾吏部尚書李默。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was the first to impeach Minister of Personnel Li Mo.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs and was the first to impeach Minister of Personnel Li Mo.

sentences.zh: 帝方顧默厚，不問。

translations.literal: The emperor was then looking upon Mo with great favor and took no action.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then showing Li Mo great favor and took no action.

sentences.zh: 出核陜西軍儲。

translations.literal: He went out to audit Shaanxi military stores.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to audit military grain stores in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 劾故延綏巡撫王輪、督糧郎中陳燦等，廢斥有差。

translations.literal: He impeached the former grand coordinator of Yan-sui Wang Lun, the bureau director supervising grain Chen Can, and others; dismissals and demotions varied by degree.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the former grand coordinator of Yan-sui, Wang Lun, the bureau director in charge of grain Chen Can, and others; they were dismissed or demoted to varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 歷吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: He served through the post of chief supervising secretary of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief supervising secretary of the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝怒禮部尚書吳山，夢龍惡獨劾山得罪清議，乃並吏部尚書吳鵬劾罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry with Minister of Rites Wu Shan; Menglong disliked impeaching Shan alone and offending pure criticism, so he also impeached Minister of Personnel Wu Peng and had both dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry with Minister of Rites Wu Shan; Menglong, unwilling to impeach Shan alone and offend orthodox opinion, also impeached Minister of Personnel Wu Peng and secured both men's dismissal.

sentences.zh: 嘗上疏，言：「相臣賢否，關治道汙隆。

translations.literal: He once submitted a memorial, saying: "Whether the chief minister is worthy or not bears on whether the way of governance rises or falls."
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized: "Whether the chief minister is worthy bears directly on whether governance flourishes or declines."

sentences.zh: 請毋拘資格，敕在廷公舉名德宿望之臣，以光聖治。

translations.literal: He requested that qualifications not be rigidly adhered to and that the court be ordered to recommend publicly ministers of established virtue and long-standing reputation, to glorify sagely rule.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that seniority rules be set aside and that officials at court be instructed to recommend publicly men of proven virtue and long-standing reputation, to brighten sagely rule.

sentences.zh: 」帝疑諸臣私有所推引，責令陳狀。

translations.literal: " The emperor suspected the officials of privately having someone in mind and ordered them to state their reasons clearly.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor suspected the officials of secretly backing particular candidates and ordered them to explain themselves.

sentences.zh: 夢龍惶恐謝罪，乃奪俸。

translations.literal: Menglong fearfully apologized, and his salary was then confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Menglong apologized in alarm, and his salary was suspended.

sentences.zh: 擢順天府丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐京察拾遺，出為河南副使。

translations.literal: Because in the capital evaluation he was picked out for censure, he went out as Henan vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Singled out for censure in the capital evaluation, he was sent out as vice commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 河決沛縣，尚書朱衡議開徐、邳新河，夢龍董其役。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River burst its banks at Pei County, Minister Zhu Heng proposed opening a new channel at Xu and Pi; Menglong supervised the project.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke through at Pei County, Minister Zhu Heng proposed cutting a new channel at Xu and Pi, and Menglong directed the work.

sentences.zh: 三遷河南右布政使。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became right provincial administration commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became right provincial administration commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年，擢右僉都御史，巡撫山東。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing he was elevated to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Longqing reign (1570) he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief with authority as grand coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 是秋，河決宿遷，覆漕糧八百艘。

translations.literal: That autumn the river burst at Suqian and capsized eight hundred grain-transport vessels.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the river broke through at Suqian and sank eight hundred grain-transport vessels.

sentences.zh: 朝議通海運，以屬夢龍。

translations.literal: The court deliberated on opening sea transport and assigned the matter to Menglong.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated reviving sea transport and put Menglong in charge.

sentences.zh: 夢龍言：「海道南自淮安至膠州，北自天津至海倉，各有商艇往來其間。

translations.literal: Menglong said: "The sea route in the south runs from Huai'an to Jiaozhou, and in the north from Tianjin to Haicang; merchant vessels travel back and forth between them.
translations.idiomatic: Menglong said: "The southern sea route runs from Huai'an to Jiaozhou, and the northern one from Tianjin to Haicang, with merchant vessels passing regularly between the two.

sentences.zh: 自膠州至海倉，島人及商賈亦時出入。

translations.literal: From Jiaozhou to Haicang, island dwellers and merchants also come and go from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: People from the coastal islands and merchants also travel that stretch between Jiaozhou and Haicang.

sentences.zh: 臣等因遣人自淮安轉粟二千石，自膠州轉麥千五百石，入海達天津，以試海道，無不利者。

translations.literal: Your officials therefore sent men to ship two thousand shi of grain from Huai'an and fifteen hundred shi of wheat from Jiaozhou by sea to Tianjin, to test the sea route—and nothing went wrong.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore dispatched men to haul two thousand shi of grain from Huai'an and fifteen hundred shi of wheat from Jiaozhou by sea to Tianjin as a trial of the route, and everything went smoothly.

sentences.zh: 由淮安至天津，大要兩旬可達。

translations.literal: From Huai'an to Tianjin, the journey takes roughly twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: The run from Huai'an to Tianjin takes about twenty days.

sentences.zh: 歲五月以前，風勢柔順，揚帆尤便。

translations.literal: Before the fifth month of the year, the winds are gentle and favorable, and setting sail is especially convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Before the fifth month the winds are mild and fair, making sailing especially easy.

sentences.zh: 況舟由近洋，洋中島嶼聯絡，遇風可依。

translations.literal: Moreover, the vessels travel by near-coastal waters, and islands in the sea lie in succession, so that if wind strikes one may take shelter.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the ships keep to coastal waters, where a chain of islands offers shelter when winds turn bad.

sentences.zh: 茍船非朽敝，按占候以行，自可無虞。

translations.literal: If the boats are not rotten and worn out, and one proceeds according to the seasonal signs, naturally one need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: So long as the vessels are seaworthy and sailing follows the proper seasonal signs, there is little cause for concern.

sentences.zh: 較元人殷明略故道，安便尤甚。

translations.literal: Compared with the old route of Yin Minglue of the Yuan, it is even safer and more convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the old Yuan dynasty route of Yin Minglue, this route is safer and more convenient still.

sentences.zh: 丘浚所稱『傍海通運』，即此是也。

translations.literal: What Qiu Jun called 'coastal sea transport' is precisely this.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely what Qiu Jun meant by 'transport by sea along the coast.'

sentences.zh: 請以河為正運，海為備運。

translations.literal: We request that the canal be made the primary transport and the sea the reserve transport.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the canal route serve as the primary channel of transport and the sea route as a backup.

sentences.zh: 萬一河未易通，則海運可濟，而河亦得悉心疏浚，以圖經久。

translations.literal: If by chance the river is not easily opened, then sea transport can supply the need, and the river can also be dredged with full attention for long-term planning.
translations.idiomatic: If the canal cannot be opened promptly, sea transport could fill the gap while the river channel receives the concentrated dredging needed for a lasting solution.

sentences.zh: 又海防綦重，沿海衛所玩愒歲久，不加繕飭，識者有未然之憂。

translations.literal: Moreover, coastal defense is extremely important; the coastal guard posts have grown negligent over many years without being put in order, and men of discernment have forebodings of trouble yet to come.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal defense is also vitally important: the guard posts along the coast have been slack for years without remedial action, and thoughtful observers see trouble ahead.

sentences.zh: 今行海運兼治河防，非徒足裨國計，兼於軍事有補。

translations.literal: Now, carrying out sea transport while also attending to river and coastal defense would not only benefit the state's finances but also help military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Implementing sea transport while also tightening coastal defense would aid the state's finances and strengthen military readiness alike.

sentences.zh: 」章下戶部，部議海運久廢，猝難盡復，請令漕司量撥糧十二萬石，自淮入海以達天津。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Revenue, which deliberated that sea transport had long been abandoned and could not all at once be fully restored, and requested that the grain transport office allocate on measure one hundred twenty thousand shi of grain to be sent from the Huai region by sea to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Ministry of Revenue, which noted that sea transport had long been discontinued and could not be fully restored at once; it proposed that the grain transport office allocate 120,000 shi to be shipped from the Huai region by sea to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 工部給銀，為海艘經費。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Works supplied silver for the expenses of the sea vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Works provided funds for the sea convoy.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The report was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 已而海運卒不行，事具《王宗沐傳》。

translations.literal: Before long sea transport in the end was not carried out; the matter is recorded in full in the biography of Wang Zongmu.
translations.idiomatic: In the end sea transport was never implemented; the full account appears in the biography of Wang Zongmu.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，遷右副都御史，移撫河南。

translations.literal: The next winter he was transferred to right vice censor-in-chief and reassigned as grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and transferred to serve as grand coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 神宗初，張居正當國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenzong reign, Zhang Juzheng held power.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenzong reign, Zhang Juzheng was chief minister.

sentences.zh: 夢龍其門下士，特愛之，召為戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Menglong was his disciple; he was especially fond of him and summoned him to be right vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Menglong was one of his protégés and a particular favorite; Zhang summoned him to the post of right vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋改兵部，出賚遼東有功將士。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of War and went out to bestow rewards on meritorious officers and soldiers in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was moved to the Ministry of War and dispatched to reward meritorious officers and soldiers in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 五年，以兵部左侍郎進右都御史，總督薊、遼、保定軍務。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, from left vice minister of the Ministry of War he advanced to right censor-in-chief and overall commander of military affairs in Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1577) he was promoted from left vice minister of the Ministry of War to right censor-in-chief with overall command of military affairs in Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 李成梁大破土蠻於長定堡，帝為告廟宣捷，大行賞賚，官夢龍一子。

translations.literal: Li Chengliang inflicted a great defeat on the Tumen tribes at Changding Fort; the emperor reported the victory to the ancestral temple and bestowed lavish rewards, ennobling one of Menglong's sons.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengliang routed the Tumen tribes in a major victory at Changding Fort; the emperor announced the triumph at the ancestral temple, distributed lavish rewards, and granted an official appointment to one of Menglong's sons.

sentences.zh: 已，給事中光懋言：「此乃保塞內屬之部，遊擊陶承嚳假犒賚掩襲之，請坐以殺降罪。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, supervising secretary Guang Mao said: "These were tribes that had submitted and been incorporated within the border defenses; Vice Commander Tao Chengyong feigned dispensing rewards to ambush them. I request that he be punished with the crime of killing those who had surrendered."
translations.idiomatic: Before long, supervising secretary Guang Mao argued: "These were tribes that had submitted and been settled within the defenses; Vice Commander Tao Chengyong had feigned a reward distribution to launch a surprise attack. He should be punished for slaughtering those who had surrendered."

sentences.zh: 」兵部尚書方逢時曲為解，夢龍等亦辭免恩蔭。

translations.literal: " Minister of War Fang Fengshi made a strained defense on his behalf, and Menglong and the others also declined the preferential ennoblement.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Fang Fengshi strained to defend the action, and Menglong and the others declined the honors extended to their sons.

sentences.zh: 及土蠻三萬騎入東昌堡，成梁擊敗之。

translations.literal: When thirty thousand Tumen horsemen entered Dongchang Fort, Chengliang defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When thirty thousand Tumen horsemen raided Dongchang Fort, Chengliang drove them off.

sentences.zh: 寧前復警，夢能親率勁卒三千出山海關為成梁聲援，分遣兩參將遮擊，復移繼光駐一片石邀之，敵引去。

translations.literal: Ningqian was again alarmed; Menglong personally led three thousand crack troops out through Shanhaiguan to support Chengliang, sent two vice generals separately to intercept the enemy, and also moved Jiguang to garrison at Yipianshi to cut them off, whereupon the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningqian was again threatened, Menglong personally led three thousand elite troops through Shanhaiguan to support Chengliang, dispatched two vice generals to intercept the invaders, and shifted Qi Jiguang to Yipianshi to block their retreat; the enemy then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 前後奏永奠堡、丁字泊、馬蘭峪、養善木、紅土城、寬奠、廣寧右屯、錦、義、大寧堡諸捷，累賜敕獎勵，就加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Reports of victories at Yong'an Fort, Dingzipo, Malanyu, Yangshanmu, Hongtucheng, Kuandian, Guangning You Tun, Jin, Yi, and Daning Fort came in succession; he received repeated edicts of commendation and was thereupon promoted to minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He reported victories in succession at Yong'an Fort, Dingzipo, Malanyu, Yangshanmu, Hongtucheng, Kuandian, Guangning You Tun, Jin, Yi, Daning Fort, and other places; after repeated imperial commendations he was promoted on the spot to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 以修築黃花鎮、古北口邊墻，加太子少保，再蔭子至錦衣世千戶。

translations.literal: For constructing the border walls at Huanghuazhen and Gubeikou, he was given the added title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and again had a son ennobled to hereditary thousand-household commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For building the border walls at Huanghuazhen and Gubeikou he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and again had a son ennobled as hereditary thousand-household commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 召入掌部務，疏陳軍政四事。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital to take charge of the ministry's affairs and submitted a memorial setting forth four matters of military administration.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the capital to head the ministry, he memorialized on four points of military administration.

sentences.zh: 尋錄防邊功，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon, in recognition of his frontier defense achievements, he was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, for his frontier service, he was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十年六月，居正歿，吏部尚書王國光劾罷，夢龍代其位。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year, Juzheng died; Minister of Personnel Wang Guoguang was impeached and dismissed, and Menglong replaced him in the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the tenth year (1582), when Juzheng died, Minister of Personnel Wang Guoguang was impeached and removed, and Menglong took his place.

sentences.zh: 逾月，御史江東之劾夢龍浼徐爵賄保得吏部，以孫女聘保弟為子婦，御史鄧練、趙楷復劾之，遂令致仕。

translations.literal: After a month, censor Jiang Dongzhi impeached Menglong for having begged Xu Jue through bribery to protect his appointment to the Ministry of Personnel and for betrothing his granddaughter to Xu Jue's younger brother as his son's wife; censors Deng Lian and Zhao Kai impeached him again, and he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, censor Jiang Dongzhi charged that Menglong had secured the Ministry of Personnel through bribery arranged by Xu Jue and had betrothed his granddaughter to Xu Jue's younger brother as a wife for his son; censors Deng Lian and Zhao Kai joined the attack, and Menglong was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 家居十九年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home nineteen years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for nineteen years before his death.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，趙南星訟其邊功，贈少保。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign, Zhao Nanxing petitioned on behalf of his frontier achievements, and he was posthumously granted Junior Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign, Zhao Nanxing appealed on behalf of his frontier record, and he was posthumously made Junior Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，追謚貞敏。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chongzhen reign, he was posthumously given the honorific epithet Zhenmin, "Upright and Perceptive."
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously given the epithet Zhenmin, "Upright and Perceptive."

sentences.zh: 楊巍，字伯謙，海豐人。

translations.literal: Yang Wei, style Boqian, was a native of Haifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei, courtesy name Boqian, came from Haifeng.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-sixth year of the Jiajing reign (1547).

sentences.zh: 除武進知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Wujin.

sentences.zh: 擢兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 操江僉都御史史褒善已遷大理卿，巍言：「東南倭患方劇，參贊、巡撫俱論罪，褒善獨幸免，又夤緣美遷，請並吏部罰治。

translations.literal: Chief Inspector of the Yangtze Guard Shi Baoshan had already been transferred to president of the Court of Judicial Review; Wei said: "The wokou menace in the southeast is acute; the coordinating officers and grand coordinators have all been punished, yet Baoshan alone escaped and moreover used connections to gain a handsome promotion. I request that the Ministry of Personnel also be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Chief inspector of the Yangtze defenses Shi Baoshan had already been transferred to president of the Court of Judicial Review. Wei argued: "The pirate threat in the southeast is severe; the coordinating officers and grand coordinators have all been condemned, yet Baoshan alone escaped censure and even secured a favorable promotion through connections. I ask that the Ministry of Personnel be penalized as well."

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，停選司俸，還褒善故官。

translations.literal: " The emperor was angry, suspended the salaries of the appointment bureau, and restored Baoshan to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was incensed, suspended the appointment bureau's salaries, and restored Baoshan to his former post.

sentences.zh: 巍既忤吏部，遂出為山西僉事。

translations.literal: Wei, having offended the Ministry of Personnel, was then sent out as Shanxi surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Having crossed the Ministry of Personnel, he was sent out as surveillance commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 已，遷參議，分守宣府。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to administration commissioner and assigned to defend Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made administration commissioner with responsibility for defending Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 寇入犯，偕副將馬芳擊斬其部長，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: When bandits invaded, together with vice general Ma Fang he attacked and beheaded their chieftain, and was rewarded with silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders crossed the border, he joined vice general Ma Fang in defeating them and killing their chieftain, and received rewards of silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 尋為陽和兵備副使。

translations.literal: Soon he became Yanghe military defense vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Yanghe vice commissioner for military defense.

sentences.zh: 擢右僉都御史，巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: He was elevated to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief with authority as grand coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 錄搗巢功，進秩二級。

translations.literal: In recognition of the achievement of storming the enemy nest, he was advanced two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: For the victory in storming the enemy stronghold, he was promoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以養母歸。

translations.literal: After a year he returned home to care for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he retired to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 歸二年，召起巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: Two years after returning, he was recalled to serve as grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was recalled to serve as grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 增補屯戍軍伍，清還屯地之奪於藩府者。

translations.literal: He replenished garrison troops and cleared and returned farmland seized by princely establishments.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt garrison forces and recovered farmland that princely estates had seized.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，進右副都御史，移撫山西。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he advanced to right vice censor-in-chief and was transferred as grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and transferred to grand coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 所部驛遞銀歲征五十四萬，巍請減四之一。

translations.literal: The courier and post station silver levied annually in his jurisdiction amounted to five hundred forty thousand; Wei requested a reduction of one quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Annual courier and post-station levies in his jurisdiction amounted to 540,000 taels; Wei asked that they be cut by one quarter.

sentences.zh: 修築沿邊城堡，檄散大盜李九經黨。

translations.literal: He repaired and built border forts and issued proclamations to break up the band of the great robber Li Jiujing.
translations.idiomatic: He built and repaired border forts and issued orders to disperse the band of the outlaw Li Jiujing.

sentences.zh: 復乞養母去。

translations.literal: He again requested leave to care for his mother and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to retire and care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，起兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong ascended the throne, he was appointed right vice minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong took the throne, he was appointed right vice minister of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年，改吏部，進左，又以終養歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, advanced to left vice minister, and again returned home for final mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Wanli reign (1574) he moved to the Ministry of Personnel, rose to left vice minister, and then retired again to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 母年逾百歲卒。

translations.literal: His mother, past one hundred years of age, died.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died at over one hundred years of age.

sentences.zh: 十年，起南京戶部尚書，旋召為工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was recalled as minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, and soon summoned as minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1582) he was recalled as minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue and soon summoned to head the Ministry of Works in the capital.

sentences.zh: 有詔營建行宮，近功德寺。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the construction of a traveling palace near Gongde Temple.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a temporary palace built near Gongde Temple.

sentences.zh: 巍爭之，乃止。

translations.literal: Wei remonstrated against it, and the project was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei objected, and the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 明年，改戶部，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and then moved to minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and then appointed minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 明制，六部分蒞天下事，內閣不得侵。

translations.literal: Under Ming institutions, the Six Ministries separately administered affairs throughout the realm, and the Grand Secretariat was not permitted to encroach.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming practice the Six Ministries each handled affairs across the empire, and the Grand Secretariat was not to intrude.

sentences.zh: 至嚴嵩，始陰撓部權。

translations.literal: It was not until Yan Song that the secretariat began covertly to obstruct the ministries' authority.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Yan Song's time did the secretariat begin quietly undermining ministerial authority.

sentences.zh: 迨張居正時，部權盡歸內閣，逡巡請事如屬吏，祖制由此變。

translations.literal: By the time of Zhang Juzheng, all ministerial authority had passed to the Grand Secretariat; the ministers hesitated and submitted business like subordinate officials, and the ancestral institutions were thus altered.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhang Juzheng's time ministerial authority had passed entirely to the Grand Secretariat; ministers approached the secretariat deferentially, like subordinates, and the ancestral system was transformed.

sentences.zh: 至是，申時行當國。

translations.literal: At this point Shen Shixing held power.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shen Shixing was chief minister.

sentences.zh: 巍素厲清操，有時望，然年耄骫骳，多聽其指揮。

translations.literal: Wei had always been strict in personal integrity and enjoyed public esteem, yet in his old age he was compliant and mostly followed Shen's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had long been known for integrity and enjoyed public esteem, but in old age he grew pliant and largely deferred to Shen Shixing.

sentences.zh: 御史丁此呂論科場事，時行及余有丁、許國輩皆惡之。

translations.literal: Censor Ding Cilü spoke on examination-field affairs; Shixing and Yu Youding, Xu Guo, and their faction all hated him.
translations.idiomatic: When censor Ding Cilü spoke out on examination-field abuses, Shixing, Yu Youding, Xu Guo, and their allies all turned against him.

sentences.zh: 巍論謫此呂，為御史江東之、李植等所攻，與時行俱乞罷。

translations.literal: Wei had Ding Cilü demoted by deliberation; he was attacked by censors Jiang Dongzhi, Li Zhi, and others, and both he and Shixing petitioned to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Wei arranged Ding Cilü's demotion; censors Jiang Dongzhi, Li Zhi, and others attacked him for it, and both he and Shixing asked to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝從諸大臣請，慰留巍等而戒諭言者，巍乃起復視事。

translations.literal: The emperor acceded to the senior ministers' request, comforted and retained Wei and the others while admonishing the critics, and Wei then resumed his duties.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the senior ministers' plea, kept Wei and his colleagues in office while admonishing their critics, and Wei returned to duty.

sentences.zh: 當居正初敗，言路張甚，帝亦心疑諸大臣朋比，欲言官摘發之以杜壅蔽。

translations.literal: When Juzheng had just fallen, the critics at court were very assertive; the emperor also inwardly suspected the senior ministers of banding together and wished the remonstrance officials to expose this in order to prevent obstruction and concealment.
translations.idiomatic: When Juzheng had just fallen, censorial voices were loud at court; the emperor also suspected the senior ministers of collusion and wanted remonstrance officials to expose it and break the wall of obstruction.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣懼見攻，政府與銓部陰相倚以制言路。

translations.literal: The senior ministers feared being attacked; the chief minister's office and the Ministry of Personnel secretly relied on each other to restrain the remonstrance faction.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful of attack, the chief minister's office and the Ministry of Personnel secretly relied on each other to curb the censorial faction.

sentences.zh: 先是，九年京察，張居正令吏部盡除異己者。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the ninth-year capital evaluation, Zhang Juzheng had ordered the Ministry of Personnel to purge all those who were not of his faction.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth-year capital evaluation, Zhang Juzheng had ordered the Ministry of Personnel to purge all opponents.

sentences.zh: 十五年，復當大計，都御史辛自修欲大有所澄汰，巍徇政府指持之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when the great evaluation came due again, Censor-in-chief Xin Zixiu wished to make a large purge; Wei followed the chief minister's intent and held back.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, at the next grand evaluation, Censor-in-chief Xin Zixiu wanted a thorough purge; Wei held the process back at the chief minister's direction.

sentences.zh: 出身進士者，貶黜僅三十三人，而翰林、吏部、給事、御史無一焉。

translations.literal: Of those who had risen through the jinshi examinations, only thirty-three were demoted or dismissed, and among Hanlin academicians, Ministry of Personnel officials, supervising secretaries, and censors there was not one.
translations.idiomatic: Only thirty-three jinshi-degree holders were demoted or dismissed, and not a single one among Hanlin academicians, ministry appointees, supervising secretaries, or censors.

sentences.zh: 賢否混淆，群情失望。

translations.literal: Worthy and unworthy were confused together, and popular sentiment was disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy and unworthy were indistinguishable, and public opinion turned bitter.

sentences.zh: 十七年夏，帝久不視朝，中外疑帝以張鯨不用故托疾。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventeenth year the emperor long did not hold court; inside and outside the palace people suspected that because Zhang Jin was not employed the emperor was feigning illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventeenth year the emperor had long absent himself from court; court and country alike suspected he was feigning illness because Zhang Jin had not been appointed.

sentences.zh: 巍率同列請以秋日禦殿。

translations.literal: Wei led his colleagues in requesting that the emperor hold court in the autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Wei led his colleagues in asking that the emperor resume court in the autumn.

sentences.zh: 至十月，巍等復請。

translations.literal: By the tenth month, Wei and the others petitioned again.
translations.idiomatic: By the tenth month Wei and his colleagues petitioned again.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，責以沽名。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and rebuked them for courting reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and accused them of grandstanding.

sentences.zh: 巍初敭歷中外，甚有聲。

translations.literal: At first Wei rose through posts inside and outside the capital and was very well regarded.
translations.idiomatic: In his early career Wei served widely at court and in the provinces and enjoyed a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 及秉銓，素望大損。

translations.literal: Once he held the appointment authority, his long-standing reputation was greatly diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the power of appointment, his standing fell sharply.

sentences.zh: 然有清操，性長厚，不為刻核行。

translations.literal: Yet he had integrity, and by nature was generous and lenient, not harsh in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he remained personally upright, and by nature he was generous and forbearing rather than harsh.

sentences.zh: 明年，以年幾八十，屢疏乞歸。

translations.literal: The next year, being nearly eighty, he repeatedly submitted memorials requesting to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, nearing eighty, he repeatedly memorialized asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 詔乘傳、給廩隸如故事。

translations.literal: An edict granted him post-horses for travel and stipend servants according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him imperial post-horses and stipend servants according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 歸十五年，年九十二而卒。

translations.literal: Fifteen years after returning home, at the age of ninety-two he died.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years after retiring, he died at ninety-two.

sentences.zh: 贈少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 李戴，字仁夫，延津人。

translations.literal: Li Dai, style Renfu, was a native of Yanjin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dai, courtesy name Renfu, came from Yanjin.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of the Longqing reign (1568).

sentences.zh: 除興化知縣，有惠政。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Xinghua and had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Xinghua, he governed with evident benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 擢戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 廣東以軍興故，增民間稅。

translations.literal: Because of military campaigns, Guangdong increased taxes on the populace.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had raised taxes on the populace to fund military campaigns.

sentences.zh: 至萬歷初亂定，戴奏正之。

translations.literal: When at the beginning of Wanli the disorder was settled, Dai memorialized to correct this.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored early in the Wanli reign, Dai memorialized to have the taxes corrected.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in successive steps to chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 出為陜西右參政，進按察使。

translations.literal: He went out as right administration commissioner of Shaanxi and advanced to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as right administration commissioner of Shaanxi and was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 張居正尚名法，四方大吏承風刻核，戴獨行之以寬。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng valued reputation and law; grand officials throughout the realm followed the trend with harshness, but Dai alone applied leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng prized strict reputation and law; regional governors everywhere followed suit with harsh governance, but Dai alone held to a lenient course.

sentences.zh: 由山西左布政使擢右副都御史，巡撫山東。

translations.literal: From left provincial administration commissioner of Shanxi he was elevated to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: From left provincial administration commissioner of Shanxi he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief with authority as grand coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 歲兇，累請蠲振。

translations.literal: In years of famine he repeatedly requested tax remissions and relief.
translations.idiomatic: In years of famine he repeatedly petitioned for tax remissions and relief grain.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital as vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 累進南京戶部尚書，召拜工部尚書，以繼母憂去。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, summoned and appointed minister of the Ministry of Works, and then departed on account of mourning for his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, was summoned to head the Ministry of Works, and then left office to mourn his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，吏部尚書蔡國珍罷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Minister of Personnel Cai Guozhen was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of the Wanli reign, Minister of Personnel Cai Guozhen was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 廷推代者七人，戴居末，帝特擢用之。

translations.literal: In court nomination seven men were proposed as replacements; Dai ranked last, but the emperor specially elevated and appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court nominated seven candidates to succeed him; Dai was listed last, yet the emperor personally elevated and appointed him.

sentences.zh: 當是時，趙誌臯、沈一貫輔政，雖不敢撓部權，然大僚缺人，九卿及科道掌印者鹹得自舉聽上裁，而吏部諸曹郎亦由九卿推舉，尚書不得自擇其屬，在外府佐及州縣正、佐官則盡用掣簽法，部權日輕。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Zhigao and Shen Yiguan held power as chief counselors. Though they did not dare directly challenge the ministry's authority, senior posts lacked personnel; the nine ministers and the censorate supervising secretaries with sealed authority were all allowed to nominate candidates themselves for the emperor's decision, and the section chiefs of the Ministry of Personnel were also nominated by the nine ministers—the minister could not choose his own subordinates. For prefectural assistants and county chief and assistant officials inside and outside the capital, the lottery method was used entirely, and the ministry's authority grew lighter day by day.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao Zhigao and Shen Yiguan dominated the government. Though they did not dare openly curtail the ministry's prerogatives, senior offices were understaffed, and the nine ministers plus the censorate supervising secretaries holding sealed authority were all permitted to nominate their own candidates for the throne to decide. Even the section chiefs of the Ministry of Personnel were put forward by the nine ministers, so the minister could no longer choose his own staff. Prefectural and county officials throughout the realm were appointed entirely by lottery, and the ministry's power dwindled by the day.

sentences.zh: 戴視事，謹守新令，幸無罪而已。

translations.literal: Dai took office, strictly observed the new regulations, and considered himself fortunate merely to avoid blame.
translations.idiomatic: When Dai assumed his duties, he scrupulously followed the new rules and counted himself lucky merely to escape censure.

sentences.zh: 明年，京察。

translations.literal: The next year came the capital evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the capital personnel evaluation was held.

sentences.zh: 編修劉綱、中書舍人丁元薦、南京評事龍起雷嘗以言事忤當路，鹹置察中，時議頗不直戴。

translations.literal: Compiler Liu Gang, Middle Secretariat drafter Ding Yuanjian, and Nanjing review official Long Qilei had previously offended those in power by their memorials; all were placed on the evaluation list, and contemporary opinion was largely unsympathetic to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The compiler Liu Gang, the Middle Secretariat drafter Ding Yuanjian, and the Nanjing review official Long Qilei had all once offended those in power through their memorials; all were marked for the evaluation, and public opinion was largely unsympathetic to Dai.

sentences.zh: 而是時國本未定，皇長子冠婚久稽，戴每倡廷臣直諫。

translations.literal: Yet at that time the succession was unsettled and the crown prince's capping and marriage had long been delayed; Dai repeatedly urged court officials to speak plainly in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the succession remained unsettled, and the crown prince's capping and marriage had long been deferred; Dai repeatedly urged his colleagues in court to remonstrate forthrightly.

sentences.zh: 及礦稅害劇，戴率九卿言：「陳增開礦山東，知縣吳宗堯逮。

translations.literal: When the harm of mining levies grew severe, Dai led the nine ministers in stating: "Chen Zeng opened mines in Shandong and Magistrate Wu Zongyao was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: When the damage wrought by mining levies grew acute, Dai led the nine ministers in memorializing: "Chen Zeng opened mines in Shandong, and Magistrate Wu Zongyao was arrested.

sentences.zh: 李道抽分湖口，知府吳寶秀等又逮。

translations.literal: Li Dao collected shares at Hukou, and Prefect Wu Baoxiu and others were again arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dao collected levies at Hukou, and Prefect Wu Baoxiu and others were arrested in turn.

sentences.zh: 天下為增、道者何限，有司安所措手足？

translations.literal: How countless throughout the realm are those acting like Zeng and Dao? Where can local officials put their hands and feet?
translations.idiomatic: How many men like Zeng and Dao are there across the empire? How can local officials possibly cope?

sentences.zh: 且今水旱頻仍，田裏蕭耗，重以東征增兵益餉，而西事又見告矣。

translations.literal: Moreover floods and droughts come repeatedly now; fields lie wasted and depleted. Added to this are increased troops and supplies for the eastern campaign, and now troubles on the western frontier are also reported.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, flood and drought strike in succession, fields lie desolate and depleted, troops and supplies for the eastern campaign keep mounting—and now word comes of trouble on the western frontier as well.

sentences.zh: 民不聊生，奸宄方竊發，奈何反為發其機，速其變哉！

translations.literal: The people cannot sustain life; evildoers are already secretly stirring—why instead trigger their provocation and hasten rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: The people can barely survive, and evildoers are already stirring in secret—why, then, deliberately trip the trigger and hasten revolt!

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No reply was received.
translations.idiomatic: " No answer came.

sentences.zh: 山西稅使張忠奏調夏縣知縣韓薰簡僻。

translations.literal: Shanxi tax commissioner Zhang Zhong memorialized to transfer Xia County Magistrate Han Xun for being remote and obscure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhong, the Shanxi tax commissioner, memorialized to have Xia County Magistrate Han Xun transferred on the grounds that his post was remote and insignificant.

sentences.zh: 戴以內官不當擅舉刺，疏爭之。

translations.literal: Dai argued in a memorial that eunuch officials should not usurp the power of denunciation and investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Dai memorialized that palace eunuchs had no right to usurp the power of denunciation and investigation, and contested the move.

sentences.zh: 湖廣陳奉屢奏逮有司，戴等又極論，且言：「奉及遼東高淮擅募勁卒橫民間，尤不可不問。

translations.literal: Chen Feng of Huguang repeatedly memorialized to have local officials arrested; Dai and others argued forcefully again, stating: "Feng and Gao Huai of Liaodong, who illegally recruit strong soldiers and oppress the people, especially must not go unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Feng of Huguang repeatedly memorialized to have local officials arrested; Dai and his colleagues argued forcefully once more, adding: "Feng, and Gao Huai of Liaodong, who illegally recruit crack troops and terrorize the populace, above all must be called to account.

sentences.zh: 」帝亦弗聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor also did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor again paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 已，復偕同列言：「自去夏六月不雨至今，路堇相望，巡撫汪應蛟所奏饑民十八萬人。

translations.literal: Soon after, he again joined his colleagues in stating: "From last summer's sixth month until now there has been no rain; famine victims line the roads; Grand Coordinator Wang Yingjiao reported 180,000 starving people.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined his colleagues again in stating: "From the sixth month of last summer until now there has been no rain; the roads are lined with the starving. Grand Coordinator Wang Yingjiao reported 180,000 famine victims.

sentences.zh: 加以頻值寇警，屢興征討之師，按丁增調，履畝加租，賦額視二十年前不啻倍之矣。

translations.literal: Added to this are frequent bandit alarms and repeated campaigns; levies by household quota increase, taxes by measured acreage rise—the tax burden is now no less than double what it was twenty years ago.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this come repeated bandit alarms and one campaign after another; levies rise with every household quota, rents increase acre by measured acre—the tax burden is now more than twice what it was twenty years ago.

sentences.zh: 瘡痍未起，而采榷之害又生。

translations.literal: Wounds have not yet healed when the harm of mining and commercial levies arises anew.
translations.idiomatic: The land had scarcely begun to recover when the damage of mining and commercial levies struck again.

sentences.zh: 不論礦稅有無，概勒取之民間，此何理也。

translations.literal: Regardless of whether mining taxes exist, they forcibly extract from the people in blanket fashion—what principle is this?
translations.idiomatic: Whether or not any mine tax is owed, they forcibly squeeze the people regardless—by what principle?

sentences.zh: 天下富室無幾，奸人肆虐何極。

translations.literal: There are few wealthy households in the realm; how far can villains' rampage go?
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households are few across the empire—how far can the villains' depredations go?

sentences.zh: 指其屋而恐之曰『彼有礦』，則家立破矣；

translations.literal: Point at someone's house and intimidate him, saying 'There is ore there,' and the family is instantly ruined;
translations.idiomatic: Point at a man's house and threaten him with 'There is ore beneath it,' and his family is ruined on the spot;

sentences.zh: 『彼漏稅』，則橐立罄矣。

translations.literal: 'He evaded taxes,' and his purse is instantly emptied.
translations.idiomatic: cry 'He evaded taxes,' and his coffers are drained at once.

sentences.zh: 持無可究詰之說，用無所顧畏之人，蚩蚩小民，安得不窮且亂也。

translations.literal: Armed with claims that cannot be investigated and employing men who fear nothing, how can the simple common people fail to be driven to destitution and rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Armed with accusations that cannot be disproved and backed by men who fear nothing, how can ordinary people fail to be driven to ruin and revolt?

sentences.zh: 湖廣激變已數告，而近日武昌尤甚。

translations.literal: Huguang uprisings have been reported many times, and recently Wuchang has been worst.
translations.idiomatic: Uprisings in Huguang have been reported again and again, and recently Wuchang has seen the worst of it.

sentences.zh: 此輩寧不愛性命哉？

translations.literal: Do these people not value their own lives?
translations.idiomatic: Do these people not cherish their own lives?

sentences.zh: 變亦死，不變亦死，與其吞聲獨死，毋寧與仇家俱糜。

translations.literal: Rebellion means death; no rebellion also means death—rather than swallow their voices and die alone, they would rather perish together with their enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Revolt means death, and so does submission—rather than die in silence alone, they would rather perish together with their tormentors.

sentences.zh: 故一發不可遏耳。

translations.literal: Thus once sparked, rebellion cannot be checked.
translations.idiomatic: Once ignited, the blaze cannot be checked.

sentences.zh: 陛下可視為細故耶？

translations.literal: Can Your Majesty regard this as a trifling matter?
translations.idiomatic: Can Your Majesty treat this as a trifling matter?

sentences.zh: 」亦不報。

translations.literal: " Again no reply was received.
translations.idiomatic: " Again there was no answer.

sentences.zh: 三十年二月，帝有疾，詔罷礦稅、釋系囚、錄建言譴謫諸臣。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirtieth year, the emperor fell ill and issued an edict abolishing mining levies, releasing prisoners, and recalling officials who had been demoted for memorializing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirtieth year, the emperor fell ill and issued an edict abolishing mining levies, releasing prisoners, and recalling officials who had been punished for remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 越日，帝稍愈，命礦稅采榷如故。

translations.literal: The next day, as the emperor recovered slightly, he ordered mining levies and commercial taxes restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, as the emperor recovered somewhat, he ordered mining levies and commercial taxes resumed as before.

sentences.zh: 戴率同官力諫。

translations.literal: Dai led his colleagues in forceful remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Dai led his colleagues in strenuous remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 時釋罪、起廢二事，猶令閣臣議行，戴即欲疏名上請，而刑部尚書蕭大亨謂釋罪必當奏聞。

translations.literal: At that time for releasing the guilty and recalling the dismissed, the emperor still ordered the grand secretaries to discuss implementation; Dai immediately wanted to submit a memorial listing names, but Minister of Punishments Xiao Daheng said release of the guilty must be reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: As for releasing the guilty and recalling the dismissed, the emperor still left implementation to the grand secretaries; Dai at once wanted to submit a memorial listing names, but Minister of Punishments Xiao Daheng held that any release of the guilty must first be reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 方具疏上，太仆卿南企仲以二事久稽，劾戴等不能將順。

translations.literal: Just as the memorial was being prepared for submission, Court of the Imperial Stud president Nan Qizhong impeached Dai and others for inability to comply, citing delay on both matters.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the memorial was being prepared, Court of the Imperial Stud president Nan Qizhong impeached Dai and his colleagues for failing to comply, citing the long delay on both matters.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，並停前詔。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and suspended the previous edicts entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and suspended the earlier edicts altogether.

sentences.zh: 戴引罪求罷，帝不許。

translations.literal: Dai accepted blame and requested dismissal; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Dai accepted blame and asked to be dismissed; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 自是請起廢者再，率九卿乞停礦稅者四，皆不省。

translations.literal: From then on he twice requested recall of dismissed officials and four times led the nine ministers in begging to stop mining levies—all went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he twice petitioned for the recall of dismissed officials and four times led the nine ministers in begging that mining levies be halted—all to no avail.

sentences.zh: 稽勛郎中趙邦清素剛介，為給事中張鳳翔所劾，疑出文選郎中鄧光祚、驗封郎中侯執躬意，辨疏侵之。
