translations.literal: Merit-review section chief Zhao Bangqing was upright and uncompromising by nature; impeached by supervising secretary Zhang Fengxiang, he suspected the move came from Selection section chief Deng Guangzuo and Verification section chief Hou Zhigong, and in his defense memorial attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: Merit-review section chief Zhao Bangqing was by nature stern and uncompromising. When supervising secretary Zhang Fengxiang impeached him, he suspected the move originated with Selection section chief Deng Guangzuo and Verification section chief Hou Zhigong, and in his defense memorial he attacked them.

sentences.zh: 御史沈正隆、給事中田大益交章劾邦清。

translations.literal: Censor Shen Zhenglong and supervising secretary Tian Dayi submitted successive memorials impeaching Bangqing.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Shen Zhenglong and supervising secretary Tian Dayi submitted memorial after memorial impeaching Bangqing.

sentences.zh: 邦清憤，盡發光祚、執躬私事。

translations.literal: Bangqing, furious, fully exposed the private misconduct of Guangzuo and Zhigong.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Bangqing laid bare all the private misconduct of Guangzuo and Zhigong.

sentences.zh: 光祚亦騰疏力攻，部中大哄，戴無所裁抑。

translations.literal: Guangzuo also sent up a memorial attacking forcefully; the ministry erupted in uproar, and Dai could restrain nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzuo also sent up a memorial counterattacking with force; the ministry erupted in uproar, and Dai could restrain no one.

sentences.zh: 御史左宗郢、李培遂劾戴表率無狀，戴引疾乞去。

translations.literal: Censors Zuo Zongyi and Li Pei then impeached Dai for setting a poor example; Dai cited illness and begged to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Zuo Zongyi and Li Pei then impeached Dai for setting a disgraceful example; Dai pleaded illness and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝諭留，為貶邦清三秩，允光祚執躬歸，群囂乃息。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to remain, demoted Bangqing three ranks, permitted Guangzuo and Zhigong to return home, and the clamor finally subsided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to stay, demoted Bangqing three ranks, allowed Guangzuo and Zhigong to return home, and the uproar finally subsided.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，妖書事起。

translations.literal: The next winter the demonic placard affair arose.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter the demonic placard affair broke out.

sentences.zh: 錦衣官王之楨等與同官周嘉慶有隙，言妖書嘉慶所為，下詔獄窮治。

translations.literal: Embroidered Uniform Guard officer Wang Zhizhen and others had a grudge against colleague Zhou Jiaqing and claimed the demonic placard was Jiaqing's work; he was sent to the imperial prison for exhaustive investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Embroidered Uniform Guard officer Wang Zhizhen and others bore a grudge against their colleague Zhou Jiaqing and claimed the demonic placard was Jiaqing's doing; Jiaqing was sent to the imperial prison for exhaustive investigation.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶，戴甥也，比會鞫，戴引避。

translations.literal: Jiaqing was Dai's nephew; when the joint interrogation came, Dai withdrew to avoid conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing was Dai's nephew; when the joint interrogation was held, Dai withdrew to avoid the appearance of partiality.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而惡之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of this and took offense.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he took offense.

sentences.zh: 會王士騏通書事發，下部議。

translations.literal: At the same time Wang Shiqi's correspondence affair broke; the matter was sent to the ministry for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Wang Shiqi's correspondence affair came to light, and the matter was referred to the ministry for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 士騏奏辨。

translations.literal: Shiqi submitted a memorial in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi submitted a memorial defending himself.

sentences.zh: 帝謂士騏不宜辨，責戴不能鉗屬官。

translations.literal: The emperor said Shiqi should not defend himself and reproached Dai for failing to silence his subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Shiqi ought not defend himself and rebuked Dai for failing to restrain his subordinate.

sentences.zh: 戴引罪，而疏紙誤用印，復被譙讓，罪其司屬。

translations.literal: Dai accepted blame, but his memorial mistakenly used the wrong seal and he was rebuked again; blame fell on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Dai accepted blame, but his memorial bore the wrong seal and he was rebuked again; punishment fell on his staff.

sentences.zh: 戴疏謝，用印如故。

translations.literal: Dai submitted a memorial of apology, still using the same seal.
translations.idiomatic: Dai submitted a memorial of apology, again using the same seal.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，令致仕，奪郎中以下俸。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry, ordered him to retire, and stripped salaries below the rank of section chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry, ordered him to retire, and stripped the salaries of all officials in the ministry below the rank of section chief.

sentences.zh: 戴秉銓六年，溫然長者，然聲望出陸光祖諸人下。

translations.literal: Dai held the Ministry of Personnel for six years—a gentle elder—but his reputation fell below men like Lu Guangzu.
translations.idiomatic: Dai headed the Ministry of Personnel for six years. A gentle, elder statesman he was, yet his standing fell short of men such as Lu Guangzu.

sentences.zh: 趙誌臯、沈一貫柄政，戴不敢為異，以是久於其位，而銓政益頹廢矣。

translations.literal: With Zhao Zhigao and Shen Yiguan wielding power, Dai did not dare differ, and thus long held his post while personnel administration grew ever more decayed.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhao Zhigao and Shen Yiguan wielding power, Dai did not dare dissent; he therefore remained long in office while personnel administration fell ever further into decay.

sentences.zh: 卒贈少保。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death he was posthumously granted the title of Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 趙煥，字文光，掖縣人。

translations.literal: Zhao Huan, style Wenguang, was a native of Ye County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huan, courtesy name Wenguang, came from Ye County.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Jiajing he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the forty-fourth year of the Jiajing reign (1565).

sentences.zh: 授烏程知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 入為工部主事，改御史。

translations.literal: He entered as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works and was transferred to serve as a censor.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三年，中官張宏請遣其黨榷真定材木，煥及給事中侯於趙執奏，不從。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wanli, eunuch Zhang Hong requested to send his faction to monopolize timber at Zhending; Huan and supervising secretary Hou Yuzhao submitted a joint memorial; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Wanli reign, the eunuch Zhang Hong requested that his faction be sent to monopolize timber at Zhending; Huan and supervising secretary Hou Yuzhao submitted a joint memorial in protest, but it was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 張居正遭父喪，言官交章請留，煥獨不署名。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng encountered his father's death, censorial officials submitted memorial after memorial requesting he be retained; Huan alone did not sign.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng was bereaved of his father, censorial officials submitted memorial after memorial asking that he be retained in office; Huan alone refused to sign.

sentences.zh: 擢順天府丞，累遷左僉都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture and rose in succession to left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture and rose in succession to left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十四年三月，風霾求言。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourteenth year, amid dust storms the emperor solicited opinions.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourteenth year, amid dust storms the emperor solicited candid opinion from the court.

sentences.zh: 煥請恢聖度，納忠言，謹嚬笑，信政令，時召大臣商榷治理，次第舉行實政，弊在內府者一切報罷，而飭戒督撫有司務求民瘼。

translations.literal: Huan requested restoring imperial magnanimity, accepting loyal remonstrance, curbing levity in expression, trusting policy decrees, summoning ministers regularly to discuss governance, implementing practical reforms step by step, abolishing all abuses within the inner palace, and instructing grand coordinators and local officials to seek out the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Huan asked that imperial magnanimity be restored, loyal remonstrance welcomed, levity in court curbed, and policy decrees trusted; that ministers be summoned regularly to discuss governance, practical reforms implemented step by step, and every abuse within the inner palace abolished; and that grand coordinators and local officials be charged to seek out the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 尋遷工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to right vice minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to right vice minister of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 改吏部，進左。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to left vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 乞假去。

translations.literal: He requested leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He requested leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 起南京右都御史，以親老辭。

translations.literal: He was recalled as right censor-in-chief in Nanjing but declined on grounds of aged parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as right censor-in-chief in Nanjing but declined on the grounds that his parents were elderly.

sentences.zh: 時煥兄遼東巡撫僉都御史燿亦乞歸養。

translations.literal: At that time Huan's elder brother Yao, vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Liaodong, also requested to return home to care for their parents.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huan's elder brother Yao, vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Liaodong, also asked to return home to care for their parents.

sentences.zh: 吏部言二人情同，燿為長子，且任封疆久，可聽其歸。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel stated the two men's circumstances were alike, Yao was the eldest son and had long served on the frontier, so he could be permitted to return.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel reported that the two men's circumstances were alike, that Yao was the eldest son and had long served on the frontier, and that he might be permitted to return.

sentences.zh: 乃趣煥就職。

translations.literal: Huan alone was urged to take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: Huan alone was pressed to take up his post.

sentences.zh: 尋召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to serve as Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 議日本貢事，力言非策。

translations.literal: On deliberation over Japan's tribute mission, he forcefully argued it was not a sound policy.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated Japan's tribute mission, he forcefully argued that the policy was unsound.

sentences.zh: 男子諸龍光訐奏李如松通倭下吏，並及其黨陳仲登枷赤日中，期滿戍瘴鄉。

translations.literal: A man named Zhu Longguang denounced Li Rusong for colluding with Japanese pirates and had him imprisoned; he also had Rusong's associate Chen Zhongdeng shackled in the noonday sun, to be banished to a malarial region when the term expired.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Zhu Longguang denounced Li Rusong for colluding with Japanese pirates and had him imprisoned; he also had Rusong's associate Chen Zhongdeng shackled in the noonday sun, to be banished to a malarial region when the sentence expired.

sentences.zh: 煥以盛暑必斃，而二人罪不當死，兩疏力爭。

translations.literal: Huan argued that in the height of summer they would surely die, and that neither man's crime warranted death; in two memorials he contested forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Huan argued that in the midsummer heat they would surely die, and that neither man's crime warranted death; in two memorials he contested the matter forcefully.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，詰責。

translations.literal: He defied the imperial will and was rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: He defied the imperial will and was rebuked.

sentences.zh: 復以議浙江巡按彭應參獄失帝意，遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: Again for his deliberation on Zhejiang touring censor Peng Yingcan's case he lost the emperor's favor and retired citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: He again lost the emperor's favor over his handling of the case of Zhejiang touring censor Peng Yingcan and retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 再起南京右都御史，就改吏部尚書，皆不赴。

translations.literal: He was again recalled as right censor-in-chief in Nanjing and immediately changed to Minister of Personnel—he attended neither post.
translations.idiomatic: He was again recalled as right censor-in-chief in Nanjing and at once offered appointment as Minister of Personnel; he accepted neither post.

sentences.zh: 家居十六年。

translations.literal: He lived at home for sixteen years.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement at home for sixteen years.

sentences.zh: 召拜刑部尚書，尋兼署兵部。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Punishments and soon also served concurrently as acting minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Minister of Punishments and soon also held concurrent charge of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 四十年二月，孫丕揚去，改署吏部。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fortieth year Sun Buyang departed and he was changed to acting minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fortieth year Sun Buyang left office, and Huan was shifted to acting minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時神宗怠於於事，曹署多空。

translations.literal: At that time the Shenzong Emperor was slack in affairs and many offices stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Shenzong Emperor had grown slack in governance, and many offices stood vacant.

sentences.zh: 內閣惟葉向高，杜門者已三月。

translations.literal: In the inner cabinet Ye Xianggao alone remained; he had shut his doors for three months already.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao alone remained in the inner cabinet; he had already kept his doors shut for three months.

sentences.zh: 六卿止一煥在，又兼署吏部，吏部無復堂上官。

translations.literal: Of the six ministers only Huan remained, and he also concurrently headed the Ministry of Personnel, so that ministry had no regular chief in office.
translations.idiomatic: Of the six ministers only Huan remained, and since he also held concurrent charge of the Ministry of Personnel, that ministry had no regular chief in office at all.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書李化龍卒，召王象乾未至，亦不除侍郎。

translations.literal: Minister of War Li Hualong died; Wang Xiangqian was summoned but had not arrived, and no vice minister was appointed either.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Li Hualong died; Wang Xiangqian was summoned but had not yet arrived, and no vice minister was appointed either.

sentences.zh: 戶、禮、工三部各止一侍郎而已。

translations.literal: The Ministries of Revenue, Rites, and Works each had only one vice minister left.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministries of Revenue, Rites, and Works each had only a single vice minister left.

sentences.zh: 都察院自溫純罷去，八年無正官。

translations.literal: Since Wen Chun's dismissal from the Censorate, there had been no regular chief for eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wen Chun's dismissal from the Censorate, the post of chief censor had stood vacant for eight years.

sentences.zh: 故事，給事中五十人，御史一百十人，至是皆不過十人。

translations.literal: By precedent there were fifty supervising secretaries and one hundred ten censors; now there were no more than ten of each.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent there were fifty supervising secretaries and one hundred ten censors; by then there were no more than ten of each.

sentences.zh: 煥累疏乞除補。

translations.literal: Huan repeatedly memorialized begging for appointments to fill the vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: Huan repeatedly memorialized begging that the vacancies be filled.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不報。

translations.literal: The emperor replied to none of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered none of them.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，遂用煥為吏部尚書，諸部亦除侍郎四人。

translations.literal: That August he was finally appointed Minister of Personnel, and four vice ministers were also appointed in the various ministries.
translations.idiomatic: That August Huan was finally appointed Minister of Personnel, and four vice ministers were also appointed across the ministries.

sentences.zh: 既而考選命下，補給事中十七人，御史五十人，言路稱盛。

translations.literal: Soon after the examination-and-selection orders were issued, seventeen supervising secretaries and fifty censors were added, and the censorial voice was said to flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the examination-and-selection orders were issued, filling seventeen supervising secretaries and fifty censorial posts, and the remonstrating voice of the court was said to flourish once more.

sentences.zh: 然是時朋黨已成，中朝議論角立。

translations.literal: Yet by then factional cliques had formed and debate in court stood opposed on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by then factional cliques had already formed, and debate at court stood sharply divided.

sentences.zh: 煥素有清望，驟起田間，於朝臣本無所左右，顧雅不善東林。

translations.literal: Huan had long enjoyed a reputation for integrity; suddenly raised from retirement, he had no prior alliances among court officials, yet he had never been friendly toward the Donglin faction.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had long enjoyed a reputation for integrity; suddenly raised from retirement, he had no prior ties among court officials, yet he had never been on good terms with the Donglin faction.

sentences.zh: 諸攻東林者乘間入之。

translations.literal: Those who attacked the Donglin faction seized the opportunity to gain access to him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who attacked the Donglin faction seized the opportunity to gain influence over him.

sentences.zh: 所舉措往往不協清議，先後為御史李若星、給事中孫振基所劾。

translations.literal: His actions and appointments often failed to accord with pure opinion; he was successively impeached by Censor Li Ruoxing and Supervising Secretary Sun Zhenji.
translations.idiomatic: His actions and appointments often failed to accord with prevailing opinion, and he was successively impeached by Censor Li Ruoxing and Supervising Secretary Sun Zhenji.

sentences.zh: 帝皆優詔慰留之。

translations.literal: The emperor each time issued gracious edicts to comfort him and retain him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Each time, the emperor issued gracious edicts urging him to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 已，兵部主事卜履吉為署部事都御史孫瑋所論。

translations.literal: Soon after, Bu Lüji, a section chief in the Ministry of War, was denounced by Sun Wei, the Censor-in-Chief who was acting as minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, Bu Lüji, a section chief in the Ministry of War, was impeached by Sun Wei, the Censor-in-Chief then acting as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 煥以履吉罪輕，擬奪俸三月。

translations.literal: Huan held that Lüji's offense was light and proposed to deduct three months' salary.
translations.idiomatic: Huan held that Lüji's offense was minor and proposed a three-month salary deduction.

sentences.zh: 給事中趙興邦劾煥徇私。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhao Xingbang impeached Huan for showing partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhao Xingbang impeached Huan for favoritism.

sentences.zh: 煥疏辨，再乞罷。

translations.literal: Huan memorialized in defense and again begged to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan memorialized in his own defense and again asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 向高言：「今國事艱難，人才日寡。

translations.literal: Xianggao said: "Now state affairs are difficult and talent grows scarcer day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao said: "State affairs are now grave, and capable men grow fewer by the day.

sentences.zh: 在野者既賜環無期，在朝者復晨星無幾，乃大小臣工，日尋水火，甚非國家福也。

translations.literal: Those in retirement have no timely recall, those at court are again few as morning stars; yet great and small officials daily pursue fire and water—this is hardly a blessing to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Men out of office wait indefinitely for recall, while those still at court are as few as stars at dawn; yet officials high and low pursue one another with daily strife—hardly a blessing to the state.

sentences.zh: 臣願自今已後共捐成心，憂國事，議論聽之言官，主張聽之當事。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that from now on all alike set aside settled minds, worry over state affairs, let remonstrators speak in debate, and let those in charge decide in policy.
translations.idiomatic: I hope that hereafter we may all lay aside settled prejudices and devote ourselves to the state's troubles—letting censorial officers speak freely in debate and letting those in charge decide in policy.

sentences.zh: 使大臣得展布而毋苦言官之掣肘，言官得發舒而毋患當事之摧殘，天下事尚可為也。

translations.literal: Thus may grand ministers fully act without the vexation of remonstrators' restraints, and remonstrators fully speak without fear of those in charge crushing them; then affairs under Heaven may still be managed.
translations.idiomatic: Then grand ministers may act without chafing at censorial checks, and censorial officers may speak without fear of reprisal from those in power—and affairs under Heaven may yet be managed.

sentences.zh: 」因請諭煥起視事，煥乃出。

translations.literal: " He thereupon asked that Huan be instructed to resume office; Huan then came out.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon asked that Huan be instructed to resume his duties, and Huan finally returned to office.

sentences.zh: 明年春，以年例出振基及御史王時熙、魏雲中於外。

translations.literal: The next spring, by annual rotation custom, Zhenji and censors Wang Shixi and Wei Yunzhong were sent to outside posts.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, under the annual rotation custom, Sun Zhenji and Censors Wang Shixi and Wei Yunzhong were transferred to posts outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 三人嘗力攻湯賓尹、熊廷弼者，又不移咨都察院，於是御史湯兆京守故事爭，且詆煥。

translations.literal: The three had once vigorously attacked Tang Binyin and Xiong Tingbi; moreover the transfer was not referred to the Censorate for consultation, whereupon Censor Tang Zhaojing upheld precedent and protested, and moreover denounced Huan.
translations.idiomatic: All three had been vigorous attackers of Tang Binyin and Xiong Tingbi; moreover Huan had not referred the transfers to the Censorate for consultation, whereupon Censor Tang Zhaojing protested on grounds of precedent and denounced Huan as well.

sentences.zh: 煥屢疏訐辯，杜門不出，詔慰起之。

translations.literal: Huan repeatedly memorialized in retort and defense, shut his door and did not go out; an edict comforted him and ordered him to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: Huan repeatedly memorialized in angry rebuttal, shut himself indoors, and refused to appear; the emperor issued an edict urging him to return to duty.

sentences.zh: 兆京以爭不得，投劾徑歸。

translations.literal: Zhaojing, failing to prevail in the dispute, submitted an impeachment memorial and went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhaojing, having failed to prevail, submitted his resignation and returned home directly.

sentences.zh: 其同官李邦華、周起元、孫居相，及戶部郎中賀烺交章劾煥擅權，請還振基等於言路。

translations.literal: His colleagues Li Banghua, Zhou Qiyuan, and Sun Juxiang, together with Revenue Bureau director He Lang, submitted successive memorials impeaching Huan for usurping power and asking that Zhenji and the others be restored to the remonstrating circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues Li Banghua, Zhou Qiyuan, and Sun Juxiang, together with Bureau Director He Lang of the Ministry of Revenue, jointly impeached Huan for abuse of power and petitioned that Sun Zhenji and the others be restored to their censorial posts.

sentences.zh: 帝為奪諸臣俸，貶烺官以慰煥。

translations.literal: The emperor for this reason deducted the officials' salaries and demoted Lang's rank to comfort Huan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor penalized the protesting officials with salary deductions and demoted He Lang's rank to placate Huan.

sentences.zh: 煥請去益力。

translations.literal: Huan's pleas to leave grew all the stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Huan pressed all the harder for dismissal.

sentences.zh: 九月，遂叩首闕前，出城待命。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he then kowtowed before the palace gate, left the city, and awaited orders.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he kowtowed before the palace gates, left the capital, and awaited the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 帝猶遣諭留。

translations.literal: The emperor still sent word urging him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still sent word urging him to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 給事中李成名復劾煥伐異黨同，煥遂稱疾篤，堅不起。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Li Chengming again impeached Huan for cutting down the unlike and clinging to the like; Huan then declared his illness grave and firmly refused to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Li Chengming again impeached Huan for ostracizing opponents and favoring allies; Huan declared himself gravely ill and steadfastly refused to return.

sentences.zh: 逾月，乃許乘傳歸。

translations.literal: After more than a month, he was finally permitted to return home by official carriage.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later, he was at last permitted to return home by official relay.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，吏部尚書鄭繼之去國。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, Minister of Personnel Zheng Jizhi left the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year of Wanli (1618), Minister of Personnel Zheng Jizhi left office.

sentences.zh: 時黨人勢成，清流斥逐已盡。

translations.literal: At the time factional power was established and the pure stream had been driven out entirely.
translations.idiomatic: By then the factions held firm sway, and the morally upright had been driven from court entirely.

sentences.zh: 齊黨亓詩教摯尤張。

translations.literal: Among the Qi faction, Qi Shijiao's power was especially overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Qi faction, Qi Shijiao was especially overbearing in his influence.

sentences.zh: 以煥為鄉人老而易制，力引煥代繼之，年七十有七矣。

translations.literal: Holding that Huan, as a fellow townsman, was old and easy to control, he exerted himself to bring Huan in to replace Jizhi; Huan was seventy-seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: Judging Huan, as a fellow townsman, to be elderly and pliable, he worked hard to install Huan as Jizhi's successor; Huan was seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 比至，一聽詩教指揮，不敢異同，由是素望益損。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he obeyed Shijiao's commands in everything and dared not differ; thereby his long-standing reputation was further damaged.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, he followed Qi Shijiao's lead in everything and dared voice no dissent, and his long-standing reputation suffered all the more.

sentences.zh: 帝終以煥清操，委信之。

translations.literal: The emperor still, because of Huan's clean conduct, entrusted him with confidence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still trusted Huan, valuing his integrity.

sentences.zh: 及明年七月，遼東告警，煥率廷臣詣文華門固請帝臨朝議政。

translations.literal: When the next year, in the seventh month, Liaodong raised alarms, Huan led court officials to the Wenhua Gate and firmly begged the emperor to hold court and discuss government.
translations.idiomatic: The following July, when alarms came from Liaodong, Huan led the court officials to the Wenhua Gate and firmly petitioned the emperor to hold audience and discuss state affairs.

sentences.zh: 抵暮，始遣中官諭之退，而諸軍機要務廢閣如故。

translations.literal: At dusk he was at last sent word by a palace eunuch to withdraw, while the various military and state affairs remained shelved as before.
translations.idiomatic: Not until evening did a palace eunuch instruct them to withdraw, while vital military and state business remained shelved as before.

sentences.zh: 煥等復具疏趣之，且作危語曰：「他日薊門蹂躪，敵人叩閽，陛下能高枕深宮，稱疾謝卻之乎？

translations.literal: Huan and the others again submitted a full memorial urging him, and moreover used alarming words, saying: "If one day Ji's Gate is trampled, the enemy knocks at the gate-tower—can Your Majesty, reclining deep in the palace on a high pillow, plead illness and decline?
translations.idiomatic: Huan and the others submitted another memorial pressing the point, warning: "If one day the enemy tramples through Ji Gate and knocks at the palace gates, will Your Majesty still lie at ease in the inner palace and plead illness to refuse audience?

sentences.zh: 」帝由是嗛焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor was thereby ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was shamed by this.

sentences.zh: 考滿當增秩，寢不報。

translations.literal: When his term review was complete he should have received a rank increase; the matter was shelved without reply.
translations.idiomatic: When his performance review came due he should have received a promotion in rank, but the memorial was left unanswered.

sentences.zh: 煥尋卒，恤典不及。

translations.literal: Huan soon died; the customary mourning honors were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Huan soon died, and the customary posthumous honors were denied.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，始賜如制。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was at last granted honors according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne were the honors granted according to custom.

sentences.zh: 熹宗初，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xizong's reign, he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Xizong (Tianqi), he was posthumously named Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 鄭繼之，字伯孝，襄陽人。

translations.literal: Zheng Jizhi, courtesy name Boxiao, was a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jizhi, courtesy name Boxiao, was a native of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十四年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the forty-fourth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the forty-fourth year of the Jiajing reign (1565).

sentences.zh: 除余幹知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yugan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yugan.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to section chief in the Ministry of Revenue and served through bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to section chief in the Ministry of Revenue and rose through the ranks to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 遷寧國知府，進四川副使，以養親歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Ningguo, advanced to vice commissioner of Sichuan, and returned home to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Ningguo, then promoted to vice commissioner of Sichuan, but returned home to care for his aging parents.

sentences.zh: 服除，久之不出。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, for a long time he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he remained out of office for many years.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十九年，用給事中陳尚象薦，起官江西，進右參政。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Wanli, on Supervising Secretary Chen Shangxiang's recommendation, he was raised to office in Jiangxi and advanced to Right Assistant Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Wanli (1591), on the recommendation of Supervising Secretary Chen Shangxiang, he was recalled to serve in Jiangxi and promoted to Right Assistant Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召為太仆少卿，累遷大理卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and was repeatedly promoted to Chief of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and eventually rose to Chief of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 東征師罷，吏部尚書李戴議留戍兵萬五千，令朝鮮供億。

translations.literal: When the eastern expedition forces were dismissed, Minister of Personnel Li Dai proposed leaving fifteen thousand garrison troops and ordering Korea to supply provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern expedition army was withdrawn, Minister of Personnel Li Dai proposed keeping fifteen thousand troops in garrison and having Korea supply their provisions.

sentences.zh: 繼之曰：「既留兵，自當轉餉，柰何疲敝屬國。

translations.literal: Jizhi said: "Since troops are being kept, grain should naturally be transport-supplied—why exhaust and wear out a tributary state?
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi said: "If we keep troops there, we ought to supply them ourselves—why drain our tributary ally?

sentences.zh: 」議者韙之。

translations.literal: " Those who joined in the deliberation applauded the point.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who debated the matter applauded it.

sentences.zh: 為大理九年，擢南京戶部尚書，就改吏部。

translations.literal: After nine years as chief of judicial review, he was promoted to Minister of Revenue at Nanjing and then immediately transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years at the Court of Judicial Review, he was promoted to Minister of Revenue at Nanjing and then immediately transferred to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，吏部尚書趙煥罷。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, Minister of Personnel Zhao Huan was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Wanli (1613), Minister of Personnel Zhao Huan was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 時帝雖倦勤，特謹銓部選，久不除代。

translations.literal: At the time, though the emperor was weary of diligence, he was especially careful about Ministry of Personnel selections and for a long time did not appoint a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor had grown negligent of routine business, he remained careful about appointments through the Ministry of Personnel and for a long time filled Huan's post with no successor.

sentences.zh: 以繼之有清望，明年二月，乃召之代煥。

translations.literal: Because Jizhi enjoyed a reputation for integrity, in the second month of the next year he was summoned to replace Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zheng Jizhi enjoyed a reputation for integrity, he was summoned the following February to replace Huan.

sentences.zh: 繼之久處散地，無黨援。

translations.literal: Jizhi had long been in inactive posts and had no factional backing.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jizhi had long languished in undemanding posts and had no factional backing.

sentences.zh: 然是時言路持權，齊、楚、浙三黨尤橫，大僚進退，惟其喜怒。

translations.literal: Yet at this time the remonstrating circuit held power; the Qi, Chu, and Zhe factions were especially overbearing, and the advancement and dismissal of grand officials depended on their pleasure and anger alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by then the censorial officers held real power; the Qi, Chu, and Zhe factions were especially overbearing, and the rise and fall of senior officials depended entirely on their whim.

sentences.zh: 繼之故楚產，習楚人議論，且年八十余，耄而憒，遂一聽黨人意指。

translations.literal: Jizhi was originally a man of Chu, accustomed to Chu men's discourse; moreover he was over eighty, senile and muddled, and therefore obeyed the factions' intentions entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jizhi was a native of Chu, steeped in its factional rhetoric; he was also over eighty, senile and confused, and so deferred entirely to the factions' will.

sentences.zh: 文選郎中王大智者，繼之所倚信。

translations.literal: Wang Dazhi, bureau director of the Appointment Bureau, was one in whom Jizhi placed reliance and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dazhi, director of the Appointment Bureau, was the man Zheng Jizhi relied on most.

sentences.zh: 其秋以年例出御史宋、潘之祥，給事中張鍵，南京給事中張篤敬於外，皆嘗攻湯賓尹、熊廷弼者也。

translations.literal: That autumn, by annual rotation custom, Censors Song and Pan Zhixiang, Supervising Secretary Zhang Jian, and Nanjing Supervising Secretary Zhang Dujing were sent outside—all had once attacked Tang Binyin and Xiong Tingbi.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, under the annual rotation custom, Censors Song and Pan Zhixiang, Supervising Secretary Zhang Jian, and Nanjing Supervising Secretary Zhang Dujing were transferred to outside posts—all men who had once vigorously attacked Tang Binyin and Xiong Tingbi.

sentences.zh: 時定制，科道外遷必會都察院吏科，繼之不令與聞。

translations.literal: At the time the established rule was that when censorial officials were transferred outside, the Censorate and the Ministry of Personnel's personnel section must be consulted; Jizhi did not allow them to hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: By established custom, transfers of censorial officials required consultation with the Censorate and the Ministry of Personnel's personnel section; Zheng Jizhi did not permit them to be informed.

sentences.zh: 比考選科道，中書舍人張光房，知縣趙運昌、張廷拱、曠鳴鸞、濮中玉當預，而持議頗右於玉立、李三才，遂見抑，改授部曹。

translations.literal: When censorial posts were examined and selected, Secretariat drafter Zhang Guangfang and magistrates Zhao Yunchang, Zhang Tinggong, Kuang Mingluan, and Pu Zhongyu should have been included; but because their positions leaned somewhat toward Yu Li and Li Sancai, they were suppressed and reassigned as ministry clerks.
translations.idiomatic: When censorial posts came up for selection, Secretariat drafter Zhang Guangfang and magistrates Zhao Yunchang, Zhang Tinggong, Kuang Mingluan, and Pu Zhongyu should have been among the candidates; but because they were perceived as leaning toward Yu Li and Li Sancai, they were passed over and reassigned to ministry clerkships.

sentences.zh: 大智同官趙國琦以為言。

translations.literal: Dazhi's colleague Zhao Guoqi spoke out on this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guoqi, a colleague of Wang Dazhi, raised an objection.

sentences.zh: 大智怒，構於繼之逐之去。

translations.literal: Dazhi was angry and framed him before Jizhi to have him driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dazhi flew into a rage and maneuvered through Zheng Jizhi to have him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 由是御史孫居相、張五典、周起元等援年例故事以爭，且為光房等五人稱枉，吏科都給事中李瑾亦以失職抗疏劾大智。

translations.literal: Thereupon censors Sun Juxiang, Zhang Wudian, Zhou Qiyuan, and others invoked the annual rotation precedent to protest, and moreover pleaded that Guangfang and the other four had been wronged; Li Jin, supervising secretary of the personnel section, also impeached Dazhi by forceful memorial for dereliction of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Sun Juxiang, Zhang Wudian, and Zhou Qiyuan thereupon protested on grounds of the annual rotation precedent and argued that Zhang Guangfang and the other four had been wronged; Li Jin, chief supervising secretary of the personnel section, also submitted a forceful memorial impeaching Wang Dazhi for abuse of office.

sentences.zh: 御史唐世濟則右吏部，詆居相等。

translations.literal: Censor Tang Shiji, on the other hand, sided with the Ministry of Personnel and denounced Juxiang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tang Shiji, by contrast, sided with the Ministry of Personnel and denounced Sun Juxiang and his allies.

sentences.zh: 居相、瑾怒，交章劾世濟。

translations.literal: Juxiang and Jin were angry and submitted successive memorials impeaching Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Juxiang and Li Jin angrily submitted joint memorials impeaching Tang Shiji.

sentences.zh: 給事中、御史復助世濟排擊居相。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries and censors again helped Shiji in attacking and expelling Juxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Other supervising secretaries and censors again rallied to Tang Shiji and pressed their attack on Sun Juxiang.

sentences.zh: 居相再疏力攻大智，大智乃引疾去。

translations.literal: Juxiang again memorialized with force to attack Dazhi; Dazhi then pleaded illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Juxiang submitted another forceful memorial attacking Wang Dazhi, who then pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 繼之亦覺其非，不為辯。

translations.literal: Jizhi also realized this was wrong and made no defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jizhi recognized the injustice but offered no defense.

sentences.zh: 至明年二月，胡來朝為文選，出兵科都給事中張國儒、御史馬孟禎、徐良彥於外，復不咨都察院、吏科。

translations.literal: By the second month of the next year, Hu Laichao became director of the Appointment Bureau and sent out Chief Supervising Secretary of the military circuit Zhang Guoru and censors Ma Mengzhen and Xu Liangyan to outside posts, again without consulting the Censorate or the personnel section.
translations.idiomatic: The following February, with Hu Laichao as director of the Appointment Bureau, Chief Supervising Secretary Zhang Guoru and Censors Ma Mengzhen and Xu Liangyan were transferred to outside posts—again without consulting the Censorate or the personnel section.

sentences.zh: 國儒已陪推京卿，法不當出外；

translations.literal: Guoru had already been included in the recommendation list for capital chief ministers; by law he should not have been sent outside;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoru had already been nominated for a capital chief ministership and by regulation should not have been sent outside;

sentences.zh: 孟禎、良彥則素忤黨人，故來朝抑之。

translations.literal: Mengzhen and Liangyan, on the other hand, had long offended the faction members; therefore Laichao suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Mengzhen and Xu Liangyan, meanwhile, had long antagonized the factions—hence Hu Laichao's move to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 繼之不能禁。

translations.literal: Jizhi could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jizhi was powerless to stop it.

sentences.zh: 時居相等已去國，獨瑾再爭，詆繼之、來朝甚力。

translations.literal: At the time Juxiang and the others had already left the capital; Jin alone contested again and denounced Jizhi and Laichao with great force.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Juxiang and his allies had already left the capital; Li Jin alone continued to protest, denouncing Zheng Jizhi and Hu Laichao in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 來朝等不能難，其黨思以眾力勝之，於是諸御史群起攻瑾。

translations.literal: Laichao and the others could not refute him; their faction thought to overcome him by mass force, and thereupon the various censors rose in a body to attack Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Laichao and his allies could not refute him; their faction resolved to overwhelm him by numbers, and the allied censors launched a collective attack on Li Jin.

sentences.zh: 瑾爭之強，疏三上。

translations.literal: Jin contested with great force, memorializing three times.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jin fought back fiercely, submitting three memorials in succession.

sentences.zh: 來朝等亦三疏詆訐，詞頗窮。

translations.literal: Laichao and the others also submitted three denunciatory memorials; their language grew rather exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Laichao and his allies replied with three denunciatory memorials of their own, their arguments growing increasingly thin.

sentences.zh: 來朝乃言：「年例協贊之旨，實秉國者調停兩袒，非可為制，乞改前令從事。

translations.literal: Laichao then said: "The purpose of the annual rotation custom of joint assent was in truth for those holding state power to mediate between both sides—it cannot serve as a fixed rule; I beg that the previous order be changed and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Laichao then argued: "The annual rotation's requirement of joint consultation was meant only as a compromise by those in power—it was never meant as a binding rule. I petition that the earlier order be revised.

sentences.zh: 」帝一無所處分。

translations.literal: " The emperor disposed of nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took no action whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 瑾方奉使，自引去。

translations.literal: Jin was then on a mission and withdrew on his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jin, who was then away on an official mission, resigned on his own initiative.

sentences.zh: 其秋，給事中梅之煥、御史李若星、張五典年例外轉，所司復不預聞。

translations.literal: That autumn, Supervising Secretary Mei Zhihuan and censors Li Ruoxing and Zhang Wudian were rotated outside the annual custom; the responsible offices again were not forewarned.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, Supervising Secretary Mei Zhihuan and Censors Li Ruoxing and Zhang Wudian were transferred outside the usual rotation—and again the responsible offices were not consulted in advance.

sentences.zh: 吏科韓光裕、御史徐養量稍言之，然勢孤，竟不能爭也。

translations.literal: Han Guangyu of the personnel section and Censor Xu Yangliang spoke slightly on the matter, but their force was isolated and in the end they could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Han Guangyu of the personnel section and Censor Xu Yangliang raised mild objections, but they stood alone and ultimately could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 時縉雲李鋕以刑部尚書兼署都察院，亦浙黨所推轂。

translations.literal: At the time Li Zhi of Jinyun served as Minister of Justice while also acting as head of the Censorate; he too was propelled by the Zhe faction.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Zhi of Jinyun served as Minister of Justice while also acting head of the Censorate—another figure the Zhe faction had installed.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，大計京官，繼之與鋕司其事，考功郎中趙士諤、給事中徐紹吉、御史韓浚佐之。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, at the grand evaluation of capital officials, Jizhi and Zhi directed the matter; Evaluation Bureau director Zhao Shie, Supervising Secretary Xu Shaoji, and Censor Han Jun assisted.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year of Wanli (1617), at the grand evaluation of capital officials, Zheng Jizhi and Li Zhi oversaw the proceedings, assisted by Bureau Director Zhao Shie, Supervising Secretary Xu Shaoji, and Censor Han Jun.

sentences.zh: 所去留悉出紹吉等意，繼之受成而已。

translations.literal: Who was dismissed or retained all came from Shaoji and the others' intentions; Jizhi merely accepted the completed decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Decisions on who would stay and who would go rested entirely with Xu Shaoji and his allies; Zheng Jizhi simply ratified their choices.

sentences.zh: 一時與黨人異趣者，貶黜殆盡，大僚則中以拾遺，善類為空。

translations.literal: For a time those of differing inclinations from the faction members were demoted and dismissed almost entirely; grand officials were hit with petty impeachments, and the good were emptied out.
translations.idiomatic: Within a short time, virtually everyone at odds with the factions was demoted or dismissed; senior officials were brought down on petty charges, and the ranks of the worthy were emptied out.

sentences.zh: 繼之以篤老累疏乞休，帝輒慰留不允。

translations.literal: Jizhi, citing advanced age and infirmity, repeatedly memorialized begging to retire; the emperor each time comforted him and would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Citing age and infirmity, Zheng Jizhi repeatedly petitioned to retire; each time the emperor urged him to stay and refused his request.

sentences.zh: 明年春，稽首闕下，出郊待命。

translations.literal: The next spring he kowtowed below the palace gate, left the suburbs, and awaited orders.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he kowtowed before the palace gates, withdrew to await orders outside the city.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，命乘傳歸。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he ordered him to return home by official relay.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of this, the emperor permitted him to return home by official relay.

sentences.zh: 又數年卒，年九十二。

translations.literal: Several years later he died, aged ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died several years later, at the age of ninety-two.

sentences.zh: 贈少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：張瀚、王國光、梁夢龍皆以才辦稱，楊巍、趙煥、鄭繼之亦負清望，及秉銓政，蒙詬議焉。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Zhang Han, Wang Guoguang, and Liang Menglong were all famed for talent and efficiency; Yang Wei, Zhao Huan, and Zheng Jizhi also bore reputations for integrity—yet once they held control of appointments, they suffered reviling criticism.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Zhang Han, Wang Guoguang, and Liang Menglong were all praised for their administrative ability; Yang Wei, Zhao Huan, and Zheng Jizhi likewise enjoyed reputations for integrity—yet once they wielded control over appointments, they fell under bitter censure.

sentences.zh: 於時政府參懷，言路脅制，固積重難返，然以公滅私之節，諸人蓋不能無愧雲。

translations.literal: At the time the chief ministers were divided in counsel and the remonstrating circuit coerced and constrained; this was indeed a weight accumulated long and hard to reverse—yet as to the integrity of subordinating private interest to public duty, these men presumably could not be without shame.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the chief ministers were at odds and the censorial officers wielded coercive power—a long-festering ill, difficult to reverse. Yet measured against the standard of putting public duty above private interest, these men can hardly have been without a sense of shame.
